walkthroughs.body_html:
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

This endothermic reaction needs light. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy. Glucose is used for respiration, growth and stored as starch.

Waxy cuticle stops water loss. Palisade cells packed with chloroplasts maximise photosynthesis. Spongy mesophyll has air spaces for gas exchange.

Stomata on the underside open and close — controlled by guard cells.

Xylem: dead, hollow tubes with lignin. Water moves up by transpiration pull.

Phloem: living cells. Sugars move from source (leaves) to sink (roots, fruits) — translocation.

mcqs.q: Which structure absorbs light energy in plants?
options: Chlorophyll
Cellulose
Mitochondria
Ribosomes

mcqs.q: Which tissue carries sugars around a plant?
options: Phloem
Xylem
Cuticle
Stomata

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.

mcqs.q: How many CO₂ molecules make one glucose in photosynthesis?
A student measures water uptake by a leafy shoot in still air, then in front of a fan. Uptake increases with the fan on. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Air movement increases the rate of transpiration.
Wind reduces evaporation from the leaves.
Water moves down from leaves to roots in wind.
Transpiration stops when air moves.

mcqs.q: Which tissue transports sugars made in the leaves to other parts of the plant?
options: Phloem
Xylem
Epidermis
Stomata

mcqs.q: Guard cells open and close the stomata. When a plant is short of water, the stomata usually:
options: Close, to reduce water loss
Open wider, to lose more water
Turn into root hair cells
Stop the leaf from respiring

mcqs.q: Why are most stomata found on the lower surface of a leaf?
options: It reduces water loss because the lower surface is cooler and shadier.
The upper surface cannot exchange gases.
Sugars are made only on the lower surface.
The lower surface receives the most light.
